briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Detroit Brands Grow Through the Cracks While DC Clears a Path to Schedule III
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finding real wins this week — from a scrappy Detroit flower brand going viral to Bay City turning weed tax into homeless shelter beds — even as regulators drop record fines and the 24% wholesale tax fight grinds toward trial. Nationally, the DEA reopened its Schedule III registration portal and Compass Pathways opened a U.S. commercial office for its 2027 psilocybin launch, signaling real momentum even as the broader rescheduling hearing hits another procedural pause.

local.text: Ex-caregivers turn scrappy Zasso into a Detroit cult brand — A small Southwest Detroit grow is selling top-shelf flower for about $100 an ounce under a name that, in Japanese, nods to the weeds that push up through sidewalk cracks.

Bay City turns weed tax into warm beds — Commissioners are set to vote on allocating $150,000 a year in marijuana tax revenue to keep the Good Samaritan Rescue Mission drop-in center open, a facility that has served more than 250 people.

Governor candidate pledges to kill the wholesale tax — GOP hopeful John James, once rated D- by NORML, has pledged to repeal the 24% wholesale tax after industry executives wrote him roughly $90,000 in checks this summer.
Michigan brands roll out spooky Croptober drops — Statewide cultivators are releasing Halloween-themed products as harvest season peaks, including novelty funeral-style pre-rolls from Voodoo.

Record fines hit bad actors while tax suit heads to trial — Regulators tied the state's largest-ever cannabis fines in one week, revoking 20 grow licenses from a company caught shipping dirt as flower, even as MiCIA's wholesale-tax lawsuit moves toward a September trial that could still deliver relief.

national.text: DEA reopens Schedule III registration door — The agency's Diversion Control Division launched a new Form 225 application process so medical cannabis manufacturers, distributors and labs that missed the original 60-day window can still register under the Controlled Substances Act.

Rescheduling hits a pause, not a dead end — A DEA judge stayed the adult-use Schedule III hearing over a new GAO report, but medical marijuana rescheduling is already final, and the government must respond by Oct. 13.

Compass Pathways opens U.S. hub for 2027 psilocybin launch — The company celebrated a ribbon-cutting for a new Jersey City office built to staff commercial readiness for COMP360 ahead of an anticipated first-half-2027 launch.
Vireo expands Colorado footprint with $49M deal — Vireo Growth closed its acquisition of 17 PharmaCann Colorado dispensaries, pushing its retail count in the state to 56 locations.

Institutional capital is flowing back into cannabis — Curaleaf's Boris Jordan told the Cannabis Capital Conference that 'serious capital' is returning to scaled operators, months after Trulieve's historic NYSE uplisting opened the door for major-exchange cannabis stocks.
